rule: ruling:sam-2026-10-07 claims 1 and 8: the real service changes to match Design Release 2.1, whose return query sends the user back to the page they opened the address from (a picker on the notification journey); claim 10: a real cross-service constraint the prototype cannot express (the animals frontend is on another origin, repo-tests-p5-001) overrides the prototype only as far as it must, so the prototype's single-/ rule is kept and extended to the one other origin the journey lives on, never to any origin; claims 12 and 13 keep it from being a question, since no DR1 judgement covers it (the DR1 backlog left the link-out route open) and the ruling's weighing settles it.
outcome: The prototype's return query is adopted, shaped by the cross-origin constraint: INS honours a return that starts with a single / as an INS page, as the prototype does, and an absolute URL whose origin exactly equals the configured animals frontend origin, so a user who opens an address from an animals journey page goes back to it; anything else falls back to the list (view page) or the view page (delete page). Locally, on the compose stack and in CDP the allowed origin is each environment's animals frontend base URL; in the INS stub mode only same-origin paths are honoured. Today's always-back-to-the-list behaviour is replaced.
